display.purpose: The one statement a section is built around; light and wide. The closing statement may reach the 6rem ceiling at weight 200, width 118.

headline.purpose: Section headings, the bench caption, lightbox and Oficina titles.

title.purpose: Names of parts and pieces; 1.5rem for process steps, 2rem for the ateliê step heading.

body.purpose: Reading text at normal width, measured at 34-62ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase voice of things a hand operates: buttons, arrow links, the menu, tabs, field labels.

print.purpose: Uppercase voice of the watch itself: the crown's label, windows, readouts, currency; 0.75-0.8rem, 0.18-0.24em.

numeral.purpose: Prices and large readout figures, tabular.

shadows.name: case
shadows.purpose: The round case that appears when the dial becomes a watch; scales with the head size.

shadows.name: showcase
shadows.purpose: A dial presented on lacquer; drawn watches take the same fall as filter: drop-shadow(0 30px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, .5)).

shadows.name: recessed-well
shadows.purpose: Opaline sub-dials holding the movement demos.

shadows.name: window
shadows.purpose: Date and beat windows cut into a dial.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: The toast, the only floating interface with a shadow.

motion.name: ferraroOut
motion.purpose: House out-curve (CSS --ease-out, GSAP CustomEase ferraroOut): everything that arrives, reveals, hovers.

motion.name: ferraroInOut
motion.purpose: House in-out curve (CSS --ease-in-out, GSAP ferraroInOut): what travels across the screen: the lacquer opening, the hands' sweep to now, the menu circle.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Work-surface settle (CSS --ease): ateliê/Oficina entrance (0.6s fade), stack transforms (0.9s), night-mode filter and lume.

motion.name: beat
motion.purpose: One clock: every cue of the full opening sits on the 1/8 s grid; staggers are 1/64 s (minute ticks), 1/16 s (batons), 1/8 s (headline lines, crown), 1/4 s (sub-line and hint).

motion.name: seconds-step
motion.value: continuous sweep (1 step/s under reduced motion)
motion.purpose: The homepage seconds hand glides every frame; hours and minutes advance once a second. The movement demos keep their real beats (1 and 6 per second).

motion.name: scrub
motion.purpose: Pinned scroll scenes are scrubbed: the dial pullback over 3.2 viewport heights (2.6 portrait), the loupe over 1.2.

motion.name: bezel-click
motion.purpose: The bezel turns in half-minute clicks (20 clicks) while the dial becomes a watch.

motion.name: hover-ink
motion.purpose: Colour and border changes on hover and selection.

motion.name: hover-travel
motion.purpose: Small horizontal travel on hover; never lift.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons, choices, toggles and colour fields on press; the hold-to-wind button does not shrink.

motion.name: lacquer-retint
motion.purpose: The ground follows a newly chosen lacquer.

motion.name: light-follow
motion.value: exponential smoothing, rate 4/s; touch drift ±22° over ~16s
motion.purpose: The conic sheen turns toward the pointer angle; on touch it drifts on its own.

motion.name: reveal-mask
motion.purpose: Section headings rise out of a mask.

motion.name: reveal-window
motion.purpose: Product photographs open as a window.

motion.name: reveal-list
motion.purpose: Lists of peers (movements) arrive in sequence.

motion.name: reveal-chars
motion.purpose: The closing statement rises letter by letter without breaking words.

motion.name: circle-open
motion.value: clip-path circle from pivot; menu 0.6s ferraroInOut open, 0.35s power2.in close
motion.purpose: Large state changes open from their pivot (arbor, menu button, loupe).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transitions 0.15s, animations 0.2s single iteration, no travel, static layout
motion.purpose: Complete and calm: pins release, fades and colour changes stay.

components.name: Crown
components.description: The primary control: a knurled bronze crown beside a print-voice label underlined in seconds-hand gold; pushes into the case on hover and press.
components.html: Monte o seu

narrative.overview:
The interface is a watch dial seen from above, and it runs. Its palette is a forest: earthy green, a touch of gold, brown (the owner's request of 2026-10-19). Dark grounds are fumé lacquer, moss green by default and any hue on demand: lit at the centre, smoked almost to black at the edges, brushed with warm sunburst rays that catch a sheen following the pointer. Walnut and leather brown is the second dark ground. Everything that speaks is printed the way a dial is printed, in ivory Saira opened wide, with a pale sage for secondary print and a single gold borrowed from the seconds hand. The metal is warm: a bronze case and crown, gilt indices and hands. Linen, the quiet dial, carries the passages that are read rather than felt, in walnut ink: specifications, prices, the process.

Ornament is always a watch part. The crown is the primary control, the date window is the counter, minute-track rules divide, round sub-dials hold the movement demos and the step markers, and callouts orbit a part on a leader line that ends in an applied baton. The site refuses the category default of a product-photo hero with a headline and a discover button: the first screen of a persuade surface carries no buttons, only the dial and its crown, and photographs arrive later as evidence of real pieces and the bench. Density follows the surface: one idea per screen and a long section rhythm where the site persuades; practical linen panels with a lacquer showcase for the live watch in the ateliê virtual and the Oficina.

The One Clock Rule. The drawn watches tell the visitor's own time. On the homepage dial the seconds hand sweeps without stopping (the owner asked for fluid motion on 2026-10-19); the movement demos keep their real beats, because there the beat is the lesson. The opening's staggers are cued on a 1/8 s grid. Beyond it, two house curves divide the work (an out-curve for what arrives, an in-out curve for what travels across the screen), scroll scenes are scrubbed rather than fired, and each kind of content has its own reveal; the 1/8 s grid binds the opening's staggers, while reveals and hovers run free on the house curves.
keyCharacteristics: Fumé lacquer grounds, moss green by default: radial light falloff, warm sunburst rays, a pointer-following sheen, any hue on demand; walnut as the second dark ground.
One family, three widths: Saira light and wide for display, normal for reading, 125% capitals for dial print.
One accent, the seconds-hand gold, kept hand-sized; bronze and gilt are the watch's metal, not accents; lume green only at night.
Linen for the quiet passages, read in walnut ink.
Watch parts as components: crown, date window, minute track, sub-dials, applied batons.
One clock: a sweeping seconds hand on the visitor's time, openings staggered on a 1/8 s grid, scrubbed scroll scenes, motion that never repaints, and a complete static page under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Clock Rule
rules.body: The drawn watches tell the visitor's own time. On the homepage dial the seconds hand sweeps without stopping (the owner asked for fluid motion on 2026-10-19); the movement demos keep their real beats, because there the beat is the lesson. The opening's staggers are cued on a 1/8 s grid. Beyond it, two house curves divide the work (an out-curve for what arrives, an in-out curve for what travels across the screen), scroll scenes are scrubbed rather than fired, and each kind of content has its own reveal; the 1/8 s grid binds the opening's staggers, while reveals and hovers run free on the house curves.

rules.name: The Seconds-Hand Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold is the only accent and it stays hand-sized: a hand, a 1px underline, a focus ring, a pin, a dot, a meter, one word or figure. Never a button, a panel, a tag face or display type; the only accent fill is the browser's text selection. On linen, or whenever gold is text, it is Gold Ink. Bronze and gilt are the watch's metal, worn only by watch parts; they never stand in for the accent in the page.

rules.name: The Any-Hue Rule
rules.body: The lacquer is a variable. A chosen colour re-tints the ground by mixing it toward Night Ground (#090e08), 80% for the field and 45% for its highlight, and the typed `--cq`/`--cq-hi` properties carry the change over 1.1s. Moss is the house lacquer and the ateliê's starting watch (the hero watch); the colours of a customer's drawn watch belong to the customer and never count against the palette.

rules.name: The Ivory-On-The-Dial Rule
rules.body: Whatever is printed on a dial's face is Ivory Print, secondary lines included; Sage Print reads only on the field, never on the lacquer of a dial.

rules.name: The Night-Only Lume Rule
rules.body: Lume green exists only at night and only on lume-bearing parts. It changes the fill; it never blooms into a glow. By day lume is cream paint.

rules.name: The Two-Voices Rule
rules.body: Uppercase has two voices and they never swap. Print is for words that belong to the watch: the crown's label, windows, readouts, currency. Label is for things a hand operates in the page: buttons, links, tabs, menus, field labels. Neither voice is ever a kicker above a heading.

rules.name: The Printed-To-Scale Rule
rules.body: Type printed on a dial is sized from the dial's diameter, not the viewport: the hero line at 7.5% of the dial, its sub-line at 1.85% with a 0.75rem floor, date numerals at 5.2%. Dial print grows and shrinks with its dial, and still answers to the 6rem display ceiling.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: Functional text never drops below 0.75rem (12px) and text inputs never below 16px, on every surface including the ateliê and the Oficina.

rules.name: The Ring Law
rules.body: Text orbits; the centre stays clear. Labels sit on a dial's ring or around a part, joined to it by a leader line, and copy printed on a dial sits beyond the hour hand's reach. Nothing crosses the arbor.

rules.name: The Three-Grounds Rule
rules.body: Every section is lacquer, walnut or linen. Lacquer carries the story (the dial, colour, the bench, questions); walnut carries the hands section and the close; linen carries the quiet passages (movements, pieces, process) and declares itself (`data-ground="opaline"`) so the chrome can read it. Chrome reads the ground beneath it: ivory print and Seconds-Hand Gold over lacquer and walnut, walnut ink and Gold Ink over linen.

rules.name: The Lit-From-Above Rule
rules.body: One light, from above. Shadows fall down, never sideways and never as a halo; the only light that moves is the lacquer's sheen.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Buttons, fields, choice cards, photos and panels carry no shadow. Selection is an inset 1px ink frame, never lift; hover changes ink, never elevation.

rules.name: The Part-Or-Paper Rule
rules.body: If it is a watch part it is round; if it is paper or print it is square. Only small floating controls are pills.

rules.name: The Circle-Opens Rule
rules.body: Large state changes open as circles from their pivot: the lacquer spreads from the hands' arbor, the menu opens from the menu button, the bench photo opens through a loupe. Rectangles open only as windows (an inset clip).

dos: Do build every dark ground as a lit radial: lacquer is the `--ground` radial from Field Highlight through Forest Field to Night Ground; walnut is `--ground-earth`, from Leather Highlight through Walnut Ground to Burnt Walnut Edge. Lit near the centre, smoked at the edge.
Do print on lacquer in Ivory Print and Sage Print, on walnut in Ivory Print and Sand Print, and read on linen in Walnut Ink and Bark Ink.
Do make the crown the primary control of a persuade surface, labelled in the print voice over a 1px Seconds-Hand Gold underline.
Do switch gold to Gold Ink whenever it is text or sits on linen.
Do set display type light (200–300) and wide (width 112–118), reading text at weight 400 and normal width with a 1.6 line height, and every functional label at 0.75rem or more.
Do open measured content (readouts, lists, the footer) with the minute-track rule and divide everything else with 1px hairlines.
Do orbit labels around the part they name, on a leader line that ends in a baton, and keep a dial's centre clear.
Do tell sequence with the dial (quarter dials for steps, hours for the menu) and show counts in a date-style window.
Do stagger openings on the 1/8 s grid, use `cubic-bezier(.23, 1, .32, 1)` for what arrives and `cubic-bezier(.77, 0, .175, 1)` for what travels, and scrub scroll scenes (0.6) instead of firing them.
Do give each kind of content its own reveal: headings rise out of a mask, photographs open as a window, lists stagger, step dials point, the closing line rises letter by letter.

Do animate the hero only by moving or fading layers that already exist: the lacquer is painted once into a canvas and opened or closed by scale, the reflection is a small canvas that rotates, and anything that arrives piece by piece (track, batons, numerals, logo, bezel ring) is its own small layer. Nothing in a moving scene is redrawn frame by frame.
Do keep the reduced-motion page complete and calm: pins release, fades and colour changes stay, travel goes, transitions drop to 0.15s, and the seconds hand ticks once a second.
Do dress the house watch in its metal: bronze case and crown, gilt indices and hands, ivory print.
Do draw icons as inline SVG strokes (1.5–1.6 width, round caps): arrow, back, crown, plus.
Do print the stacked mark (wings, FERRARO, ATELIER) under 12 on every drawn dial, and use the horizontal lockup in chrome.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue, or let lume green appear by day or bloom into a glow.
Don't use grey for secondary text on dark grounds; Sage Print (lacquer) and Sand Print (walnut) do that job.
Don't make the accent gold a button, a panel, a tag face or display type.
Don't round paper (buttons, fields, cards, photos, panels) or square off parts (dials, wells, swatches); only small floating controls are pills.
Don't shadow paper, light anything from the side, or surround anything with a glow.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading, number content sections, or type a glyph (+, ×, →) where an icon belongs.
Don't animate clip-path, blur, filters or the children of a large SVG frame by frame in a scene; each of those repaints the screen on every frame and is what made the first opening stutter.
Don't set Sage Print on a dial's face: 4.3:1 on the mid lacquer and 1.9:1 at the lit centre. Print on a dial is ivory.
